messages:
Sophia (docs): Heads-up — I noticed the /generate OpenAPI example uses oneOf for the response but the examples embed the discriminator as "type". The JS SDK generator ends up picking the wrong variant. Also the multipart example for the upload endpoint is missing explicit boundary markers which breaks copy-paste curl snippets.

Kevin (eng-runtime): ah nice catch. Can you point me at the YAML and an example of the generated SDK output so I can repro?

Sophia (docs): YAML link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api/blob/main/openapi/generate.yaml#L700-L730 — failing SDK output: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-inference/tmp/sdk-gen-fail-2026-03-20.json

Alex (sdk): I dug into the SDK output — our generator expects a discriminator property named "variant" (and a mapping). The example uses "type" so it guesses a flat union. We can either update the example to include "variant" or add an x-discriminatorMapping in the spec. Updating docs/examples is lower risk.

Sophia (docs): Agreed, prefer docs-only fix. Proposed example change for the chat response: ```json
{ "variant": "chat", "messages": [{"role":"assistant","content":"Hi"}] }
```
And for the multipart curl snippet, give an explicit boundary example to make it copy-paste friendly:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/upload" \
  -H "Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundary7MA4YWxkTrZu0gW" \
  --data-binary $'------WebKitFormBoundary7MA4YWxkTrZu0gW\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="foo.txt"\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\n(contents)\r\n------WebKitFormBoundary7MA4YWxkTrZu0gW--'
```

Kevin (eng-runtime): SGTM. I'll open a small PR that updates the example responses to include "variant" and fixes the multipart curl example. I'll also add a short note in the migration guide so integrators know why the discriminator appears in examples now. @Alex do you want me to include a sample of the updated JS FormData snippet?

Alex (sdk): yes please — update the JS snippet to use FormData for the file upload (Node fetch + form-data) and include a short note that the generator will pick the right oneOf branch if the discriminator property is present in the example. That should make the generated examples and SDK snippets consistent.

Raymond (docs-bot): PR #4627 opened by kevin: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4627 — includes example updates, an added note in docs/migration.md, and unit tests for code sample parsing.

Luis (product): quick q — does adding "variant" to examples change any public surface or is it purely docs cosmetic?

Kevin (eng-runtime): purely docs/examples. No schema or runtime change. No customer impact.

Sophia (docs): I'll review the PR now and check staging once it's deployed. Thanks for the quick turnaround, team :tada:

Raymond (docs-bot): PR #4627 merged by Sophia (docs) — https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4627 (merge commit 0a1b2c3). Changes deployed to staging docs.redwood-inference.dev.
